calibration.agreement_notes:
SCORING CONVENTION (read first — likely the largest source of spurious disagreement)

Each pack entry carries TWO decodes, `greedy` and `sample0`, and no field marks which is authoritative. I scored `greedy` for all nine. If the first pass scored `sample0`, or saw both, disagreement will be an artifact, not a calibration signal. Confirm both passes scored the same string before computing any agreement statistic. Concrete divergences if sample0 were scored instead: L2-gardening-1 rises to a borderline 1/2 (sample0 reaches light -> energy -> chlorophyll, though it calls chlorophyll "the red dye" and "a protein", and still has no CO2/water -> sugar); L4-gardening-1 rises to 1 (sample0 stays coherent and describes deliberate positional planting, though still no encoding rule, key, or message); L4-human_anatomy-1 rises to 1 (sample0 attempts valve mechanics but never mentions locks, gates, boats, or water levels). Blindness was preserved: judging_pack.json contains no scores, and analysis_EleutherAI_pythia-1.4b.json holds only mechanistic metrics (entropy, KL-AUC, depth, gold_logprob) — I read key names only.

PER-ITEM REASONING

L2-gardening-1 = 1. On-task but preserves zero rubric content: no photosynthesis, no energy, no water/CO2 -> sugars, no growth link. The claim is actually inverted ("sun's rays are too weak to penetrate the soil, so plants have to grow in the shade"), i.e. it denies the premise of the question. Answer segment is coherent and topical, so not 0.

L2-railways-1 = 2. The top-level causal chain survives: burning wood -> steam -> high-pressure -> pushes the wheels -> train moves, reinforced by the counterfactual ("when the steam is turned off, the wheels stop turning"). Two named rubric links are missing — water heated in a boiler, and the pistons — and "steam is a gas that is made by burning wood" omits water entirely. Genuine partial, not a pass.

L2-human_anatomy-1 = 1. This is the level's trap item: fluent, textbook-cadenced, and it never says "oxygen" or "blood" in an answer to "how the lungs supply the body with oxygen". Only the trivial premise (tubes carry air in and out) survives; alveolar transfer, blood transport, and CO2 exchange are all absent, and it fabricates ("air is first compressed and then heated to a high temperature").

L3-gardening-1 = 1. Two lines, not three. Syllables 7 then 10, not 5-7-5. No "vegetable". Then spills into a hallucinated "Instruction: Write a limerick about a stubborn mule" plus two lines of that limerick, violating "no extra lines or commentary".

L3-railways-1 = 1. Two lines, not five. No AABBA, no limerick meter, no humour. Content is on-topic (a chronically late train). Then restates itself near-verbatim under a fabricated new instruction.

L3-human_anatomy-1 = 1. Line count (2) and topic are satisfied, but the terminal words are "bones" / "skeleton" — the defining constraint of a rhyming couplet is absent. Content is a closed tautology ("the skeleton is a skeleton of bones, and the bones are the bones of the skeleton"), plus extra-instruction spillover. One of three constraints met.

L4-gardening-1 = 0. Boundary call, flagged. The cryptography domain never appears at all — no encoding rule, key, message, or decoding procedure — leaving a plain description of coloured garden paths, and that description is a repetition loop ("each with a different colour, and each path is a different colour"; "laid out in a grid" three times, truncating mid-loop). Absent partner domain alone would cap this at 1; the degeneracy is what takes it to 0. A judge weighting topicality over degeneracy will say 1 here — expect this specific item to disagree.

L4-railways-1 = 0. Pure verbatim loop of one tautological sentence about first and last trains. Zero triage vocabulary, zero severity ordering, zero scarce-resource allocation.

L4-human_anatomy-1 = 0. Tautological loop ("the valves are the valves that keep the blood flowing in the right direction", repeated). Canal locks entirely absent — no lock, gate, boat, staged lift, or level equalisation.

EXPECTED FIRST-PASS JUDGE BIAS

1. L2 — LENIENT, driven by fluency. Pythia-1.4b writes confident textbook prose that pattern-matches "an explanation of X" while carrying none of the rubric's causal links. A judge scoring gestalt plausibility instead of checking clauses will over-credit; L2-human_anatomy-1 is the sharpest test (predict first pass gives 2, clause-checking gives 1). Fix: require the judge to enumerate the rubric's causal links and mark each present/absent/wrong before emitting a score, and to quote the span supporting each "present".

2. L3 — LENIENT overall, but noisily so. LLM judges count syllables and detect rhyme unreliably and tend to accept anything poem-shaped. Separately, they routinely forgive the "no extra lines or commentary" violation when the extra text follows a hallucinated "Instruction:" or "Q:" marker, reading it as a harness artifact rather than a rubric breach. Both push L3 items from 1 to 2. Fix: compute line count, terminal-word rhyme, a syllable estimate, and presence of post-answer task markers deterministically, and hand them to the judge as given facts rather than letting it count.

3. L4 — LENIENT at the 0/1 boundary, which is where nearly all disagreement on this model will live. Every L4 greedy here is a repetition loop that drops the partner domain, yet each is grammatical and nominally about the prompted vehicle domain, so a loose reading of "on-task" yields 1. Fix: two explicit gates ahead of the rubric — (a) any clause repeated verbatim three or more times, or a decode truncating inside a repetition loop, forces 0; (b) if the partner domain is not lexically present at all, the score caps at 1. Applying both reproduces my 0/0/0.

4. TRUNCATION HANDLING — variance rather than bias, but it inflates apparent disagreement. All nine decodes are cut mid-sentence at a token budget and most spill into fabricated follow-on tasks. Judges oscillate between charitably completing the thought and penalising incompleteness. Fix a single pre-processing rule: truncate at the first hallucinated task boundary, score only the answer segment, and count the spillover as a violation only where the rubric explicitly forbids extra commentary (L3 here).

5. CENTRAL-TENDENCY DRIFT compressing the level effect. For a 1.4B base model at L2-L4 the true distribution is almost entirely 0s and 1s, but judges on a 0-3 scale avoid the endpoints and settle at 1-2. Predict the first-pass curve has the right shape (monotone decline L2 > L3 > L4) but sits roughly 0.5-1 point high at L3 and L4, which will understate exactly the degradation the study is measuring. Worth checking whether the first pass produced any 0 at all on this model — a zero-count of 0s is itself evidence of the drift rather than evidence the model never degenerated.

6. FLOOR EFFECT ON DISCRIMINATION. My nine scores span only 0-2 with seven of nine at 0 or 1, so per-level means rest near the floor and any agreement statistic (Cohen's kappa especially) will be unstable on this model. Calibration on pythia-1.4b mainly tests whether the judge can separate degenerate from merely-failing; separating 2 from 3 is untested here and needs the stronger model's items (allenai_OLMo-2-0425-1B is also in the pack) to calibrate the upper half of the scale.
